title: Feature type and shape vocabulary
---

<!-- Generated by `pnpm vocabulary:sync` from @nightingale-elements/nightingale-track. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every feature record has a `type` (see [Load your own data](/protvista/your-data)). The viewer uses it to pick the feature's default colour and shape from a table built into Nightingale, the library that draws the tracks. This page lists that table as shipped in `@nightingale-elements/nightingale-track` 5.11.1, the version the viewer draws with. It is generated from that package and kept in sync by drift tests, so it cannot silently diverge.

## How a feature gets its colour and shape

The first of these that applies wins:

1. The track's `rendering.color` and `rendering.shape`. These apply to **every** feature in the track, whatever its type.
2. The default for the feature's `type`, from [the table below](#recognised-types).
3. `black` and `rectangle`.

`type` is matched without regard to case, against either the type code (`ACT_SITE`) or the longer UniProt name (`active site`).

## Types ProtVista does not recognise

A `type` outside the table is drawn as a black rectangle. The viewer shows no error or warning; Nightingale only logs the type name to the browser console. Every unrecognised type looks the same, so a track that mixes two of them cannot tell them apart.

### Worked example: a custom type

A lab marks its own hotspots with a `type` UniProt does not use:

```csv
type,start,end,description,score
HOTSPOT,132,140,Lab-defined mutational hotspot,0.87
HOTSPOT,601,612,Lab-defined mutational hotspot,0.64
```

On its own, each row draws as a black rectangle. Give the track a `rendering` block to choose the look instead:

```yaml
accession: P05067
rows:
  - id: hotspots
    label: Hotspots
    kind: features
    data: ./hotspots.csv
    rendering:
      color: '#e67e22'
      shape: roundRectangle
```

Because `rendering` applies to the whole track, it also overrides the defaults of any recognised types in the same file. Keep custom types in their own file and track so the recognised ones keep their colours.

## Recognised types

## Shapes

`rendering.shape` takes one of these 22 names. The spellings (`discontinuos`) are Nightingale's. 3 of them (`leftEndedTag`, `rightEndedTag`, `doubleEndedTag`) are declared but not drawn by the canvas track, and show a question mark instead. So does any other name: the config accepts any string for `shape`, and a misspelt one is not reported.

| Shape | Drawn as | Default for |
|---|---|---|
| `rectangle` | Stretches to cover the feature | `CHAIN`, `TRANSIT`, `PROPEP`, `PEPTIDE`, `SIGNAL`, `HELIX`, `STRAND`, `TURN`, `REGION`, `COILED`, `MOTIF`, `REPEAT`, `CA_BIND`, `DNA_BIND`, `DOMAIN`, `ZN_FING`, `NP_BIND`, `BINDING`, `COMPBIAS`, `CONFLICT`, `UNSURE`, `MUTAGEN`, `TOPO_DOM`, `TRANSMEM`, `INTRAMEM`, `VAR_SEQ`, `UNIQUE`, `NON_UNIQUE`, `RESIDUE`, `EPITOPE`, `ANTIGEN`, `PDBE_COVER` |
| `roundRectangle` | Stretches to cover the feature | — |
| `bridge` | Stretches to cover the feature | `DISULFID`, `CROSSLNK` |
| `line` | Stretches to cover the feature | — |
| `diamond` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | `METAL` |
| `chevron` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | `SITE` |
| `catFace` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | — |
| `triangle` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | `MOD_RES` |
| `wave` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | `LIPID` |
| `hexagon` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | `CARBOHYD` |
| `pentagon` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | `NON_STD` |
| `circle` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | `ACT_SITE`, `VARIANT` |
| `arrow` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | `INIT_MET` |
| `doubleBar` | Fixed-size glyph; across more than one residue a line joins its ends | `NON_CONS`, `NON_TER` |
| `discontinuosStart` | Stretches to cover the feature | — |
| `discontinuos` | Stretches to cover the feature | — |
| `discontinuosEnd` | Stretches to cover the feature | — |
| `helix` | Stretches to cover the feature | — |
| `strand` | Stretches to cover the feature | — |
| `leftEndedTag` | Not drawn — shows a question mark | — |
| `rightEndedTag` | Not drawn — shows a question mark | — |
| `doubleEndedTag` | Not drawn — shows a question mark | — |
